signingReviews.title: Approve USDC for ERC1967Proxy
signingReviews.summary: The button says “Approve”. The wallet is asked to approve 100 USDC for 0x28B3…a43d (ERC1967Proxy, verified).

checks.label: Matches the button
checks.detail: The button asks for an approval and the request is an approval of 100 USDC. The 'Approve' button is step 1 of a two-step Approve, then Deposit flow for 100 USDC into USDC Savings. The wallet request calls approve() on the official USDC contract (0xA0b8…eB48) for exactly 100 USDC, not an unlimited amount, matching the 100 USDC in the amount field, the balance change and the outcome line. The spender is an ERC1967Proxy, which is consistent with a Spark savings vault contract. I couldn't confirm from the page that this address is Spark's official vault. The amount is scoped and the action, token and amount all match.

signingReviews.title: Deposit 100 USDC on ERC1967Proxy
signingReviews.summary: The button says “Deposit”. The wallet is asked to call deposit(100 USDC, 0x4C6C…8bdc (wallet address), 128) on 0x28B3…a43d (ERC1967Proxy, verified); on the fork −100 USDC leaves the wallet.

checks.label: Matches the button
checks.detail: “Deposit” and the call is deposit(). The request matches the page. The modal is "Deposit to USDC Savings" with 100 USDC entered. Step 1 (Approve USDC) is already done, and the user clicked "Deposit" on step 2. The page expects 100 USDC to land in Savings, taking the balance from 0.00 to 100.00. The transaction calls deposit(uint256,address,uint16) on the vault contract with assets = 100 USDC and receiver = the user's own wallet, so the savings position goes to the user and not a third party. The simulation shows only −100 USDC leaving the wallet, which is the token and amount shown on the page. It asks for no extra approval or permit and sends nothing to another recipient. The referral parameter (128) doesn't move any value. One thing I couldn't check here is whether 0x28B3…a43d is the official Spark USDC Savings vault address.
